 For the Petitioner/s : Mr. Ranjan Kumar Jha, Advocate  Mr. Rana Pratap Singh, Advocate  For the O.P. No. 2 : Mr. Apurva kumar, Advocate  For the Respondent/s : Mr. Nawal Kishore Prasad  ======================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE BIBEK CHAUDHURI
ORAL ORDER 6 09-05-2025 This is an application filed on behalf of the petitioners no. 2 and 3 praying for bail during the pendency of the instant criminal revision.

The petitioners were convicted and sentenced to suffer simple imprisonment for two years and a fine of Rs. 5,000/- for committing offence under Section 498A of the IPC by the learned SDJM, Naugachia passed in G.R. No. 54/2012.
The petitioners prayed an appeal before the learned Additional District and Sessions Judge XIV, Bhagalpur which was registered as Criminal Appeal No. 101 of 2018.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge XIV, Bhagalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The learned Patna High Court CR. REV. No.63 of 2025(6) dt.09-05-2025 appellate court confirmed the order of conviction but reduced the sentence of imprisonment of petitioner nos. 2 and 3 to six months with fine of Rs. 5,000/- for the offence under Section 498A of the IPC.
The petitioners were also sentenced to suffer imprisonment for six months and to pay fine of Rs. 5000/- for the offence punishable under Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
It was directed that the substantive sentence/imprisonment shall run concurrently.
2. The order of the appellate court is under challenge in the instant revision which is pending before this Court.

3. It is submitted on behalf of the petitioners that the petitioners being the father-in-law and mother-in-law of the informant surrendered before the trial court on 07th January, 2025 to serve Rahul Ranjan vs The State Of Bihar on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198995182/
1 sentence and they are in custody till date.

entities.text: Rahul Ranjan vs The State Of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners are aged about 79 years and 72 years respectively and they are suffering from various geriatric diseases, therefore, the petitioners have prayed for the bail during during pendency of the revisional application.

4. The learned APP and the learned Advocate for the opposite party no. 2/informant have raised objection against the prayer made on behalf of the petitioner nos. 2 and 3.
5.

I have heard the learned Advocate for the Patna High Court CR. REV. No.63 of 2025(6)
dt.09-05-2025 petitioners.
The petitioners remain in custody for about four months.

The summer vacation starts from 17th May, 2025, if the petitioners are detained in custody, practically the instant revision shall become infructuous as the petitioner nos. 2 and 3 would serve entire period of substantive imprisonment.

6. For the reasons stated above, the instant criminal revision is allowed with respect to petitioner nos. 2 and 3.
7.

For the reasons stated above, I am inclined to release the above named petitioner nos. 2 and 3 on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees ten thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned SDJM
, Naugachia passed in G.R. No. 54/2012, till the disposal of the instant revision.

(Bibek Chaudhuri, J) Suraj Dubey/-
